source.geometry: primitive pill bottles, bayonet lids, pills, and weekly organizer

notes: bimanual I2RT YAM task inspired by the ABC benchmark; two matching amber 45 mm pharmacy bottles have plain ribbed white cylinder caps and wrapped Bruce Wayne pharmacy labels whose drug and large dose lines distinguish the regimens; each uses a passive spring-loaded press-and-turn 180 degree bayonet closure with a 3 mm axial seat travel and contains six certified graspable pills; the rigid 234 x 72 x 25 mm weekly organizer is centred at x 0.58 and has seven cells with independent rear hinged lids, printed day names on top, and distinct muted color tabs on a light plastic body; Monday through Friday start with one tablet beside two capsules on each cell floor, while the task fills Saturday and Sunday and closes all organizer lids; collision backed knurl ribs on both bottle grip bands transfer wrist torque; bottle bases use 0.6 sliding friction while interior walls and cap tracks retain low sliding friction; internal cap-retention contacts use a 1 ms solver time constant to resist contact-transient escape; the cap guide outer radius is 16.5 mm, clearing the spring seat during a slightly tilted two-gripper lift while preserving the press-and-turn latch; the bottles draw independently over separate exact IK safe side lanes with full yaw, the organizer draws at x 0.58, y -0.10 or +0.10, with yaw 90 or 270 degrees respectively so its lid tabs face the center; weekday pills move with it
